rules: Every defect the owner reports gets one entry here in the same PR as its detector. The detector id must exist in data/detectors.json, resolve to an implemented entry, and be present in the implementation file named by `where`; check-defect-ledger.mjs and check-ssot.mjs fail otherwise.

defects.symptom: 31 UI evidence screenshots (15 donor-parity captures and 16 process-evidence captures) were committed under docs/, so evidence lived in git history and every checkout paid for it.
The key page rendered wallet-preset chips and an equivalent preset <select> side by side.
Toolbar chips and the refresh button were cut off at 768/1280 with no way to reach them.
The Keys PAGE row showed /private-keys/bitcoin/<huge> instead of a readable page number.
The two Keys columns ended 191px apart, leaving a large empty block.
/private-keys/tron produced dozens of 502 responses from our own API; nobody saw them because the audit treated network failures as warnings.
Vanity stat cards inherited the key-page 2px padding, putting text 3px from a bordered, filled box.
Key page cards reserved far more vertical space than their content.
A public page route could be served without appearing in the UI audit route list (found: /milk-sad had 2 sub-12px exponents).
The /key info control rendered as a full bordered 44px button beside random/clear, so two identical-looking blocks read as a duplicated control.
Icon-only key actions relied on the slow native title tooltip instead of a visible hover/focus affordance.
Status pills shipped with 10.5-12px text, 7-10px inline padding, four uppercase tracking values and heights from 18 to 28px for the same concept.
Four icon-button grammars shipped 44x44 boxes with 14/15/16/18px icons and radii 7/9/10/11, so the same action read as four different products.
Form controls shipped at 38/46/52/58px high because page-local padding, hero sizes and search wrappers each invented their own height.
Inputs and selects used radii 6/7/8/10/14/16, labels ranged from 10.5 to 14px, and composite search fields removed the focus ring.
Curve and puzzle filters used two track paddings, radii 10/12, item radii 8/9 and a second compact size inside the key input card.
Cards shipped padding 8/12/13/14/15/16/18/20/22/24 and radii 0/8/11/12/14/16; the key page overrode its own card padding twice.
Stat labels were uppercase with 0.04-0.09em tracking and values ranged from 16 to 27px at weights 700/750, so the same stat strip read differently on each page.
Four table implementations used header padding 4/6 vs 8/10, cell padding 8/10 vs 8/12, and half of them were not inside a scroll shell.
Table headers shipped uppercase with 0.05-0.08em tracking at weights 700/750, so the same column label looked different on key, puzzle and directory tables.
Rows collapsed below 44px when a table had no icon action, while rows with icon buttons were taller than every neighbour.
Row actions were not consistently 44x44/radius 10/labelled across the key, browse and brainwallet rows.
The TRON row showed the raw sun amount at 18 decimals while its title showed 6 decimals, and the tx count existed only in the title.
The /key private-key field rendered as type=password, hiding the key the donor shows as ordinary text.
site.css carried a legacy blue :root above the amber token layer, so every token was declared twice and later edits depended on source order.
The legacy header shipped 38px links, 16px icons and a 40px icon utility, so the same navigation row had three target sizes and the narrow drawer targets fell below the touch floor.
Breadcrumb trails mixed plain-text slashes, raw path labels and missing trails; one page rendered an empty nav and another used the plural landmark name.
Some trails had no aria-current marker (the last crumb was a self-link), and key pages could show a raw path where the current page label belongs.
Private keys, mnemonic seeds and brainwallet directories each built their own pager wrapper, random-button modifier and disabled state; none carried a landmark label.
Pager buttons shipped radius 9 with 15px icons and no guaranteed 44px box; disabled directions were not consistently marked with aria-disabled.
The primary "Seeds" nav item linked to /seed, a single-phrase converter, while visitors expected the browsable /mnemonic-seeds directory.
Cache busting relied on hand-bumped ?v= tokens in 24 pages, coordinator templates and tests, so one forgotten bump served stale CSS or JS after a deploy.
No served page carried the donor-parity footer (FAQ, Disclaimer, Donate, Docs, GitHub, copyright, build version), so the shell ended without legal or contact links.
Empty states shipped as three page-local classes (.key-empty defined twice, .range-empty, .monitor-empty) with no shared box; error margins drifted to 10px while .error itself carried no margin.
At <=560px the phone-density rule forced a three-column grid on the account-chain directory summary, so its two Balance/Active cards left the third cell empty.
The /key info control shipped a page-local button.key-info-btn (44px box, radius 8, 16px glyph) instead of the shared .icon-button component, so icon-only actions had a second control size.
Quiet icon buttons gained a 1px hover border from the generic button:hover rule, contradicting DESIGN-SYSTEM §3.2; outline buttons also lost their line-strong border on hover.

The wallet page only accepted a pasted WIF or hex key: there was no way to generate a phrase, the page never showed one and nothing reported its entropy or brute-force strength, so a user could not judge the phrase.

A Network.loadingFailed event whose request id was not in the request map was treated as same-origin because the URL parse fell back to the base origin, so a browser-injected external request surfaced as a false http-error violation and stalled the route.

After the manual ?v= tokens were removed, assets relied on origin no-cache; Cloudflare's zone Browser Cache TTL overrode it (max-age=14400, cf-cache-status: REVALIDATED), so a returning browser kept old JS/CSS for up to 4 hours after a deploy. HTML must reference build-prefixed /a/<build>/ URLs instead of bare assets.
HEAD /rotor_wasm.wasm and every public asset/page answered 404 while GET returned 200, because only GET entered the public branch; monitors, CDNs and link checkers saw the whole site as missing.
tokens.json, the generated :root region and the frozen 95-name contract could disagree, and a var(--x) could reference a name no first-party file declares.
14 declared tokens had no first-party consumer, so dead scale steps accumulated silently between batches.
A colour role could be declared in :root without a light value, leaving light mode on the dark fallback or an implicit alias.
site.css shipped 100 literal border-radius declarations (8/12/999px and off-scale 6/7/9/11/13/14/18px) instead of the --radius-* scale.
75 raw colours in first-party CSS and 34 chain brand colours in inline styles bypassed the token layer outside the generated :root and light regions.
Page-scoped rules still overrode shared families (.key-page .notice, .puzzle-cta .btn, .seed-count-row .chip), the .key-page > .card pattern the batch-7 cleanup removed.

A component manifest could declare a variant or size class that no rule in site.css styles (for example an aspirational .btn--ghost), so the gallery and production would disagree about what the contract means.
The generated /cabinet/admin/design gallery could miss a variant, size or state declared in a manifest, so a state shipped in the contract without rendered evidence.
A gallery example could drop a required attribute (aria-label, data-tooltip, role, aria-describedby, aria-hidden), hiding an accessibility regression behind a green gallery.
A page <style> block could restyle a shared family (.card, .chip, .icon-button) and bypass the shared component contract, including the generated gallery.

The documented 56px .field--hero size never rendered: the base input:not(...) selector had higher specificity than .field--hero > input, so /key and the gallery measured 44px while the manifest and doc claimed 56px.

Every browse listing row rendered the compressed and uncompressed WIF under the hex key (163px rows, 11,036px document at /private-keys/tron) and put the WIF next to the address, while the donor keeps the WIF key-level on /key/<hex>.
Bitcoin legacy listing rows hid the uncompressed address behind a disclosure, so the row showed one address and needed a click for the second; the donor renders both address forms immediately.

Every balance line printed a zero received amount and a relative-age label, and the figures were plain text with no accessible names; the donor only prints the received pill when it is non-zero and emphasises the TX count.
Every listing row shipped a <button class="copy-btn">Copy private key</button> that `.col-key .copy-btn` set to display:none (60 dead controls per page); the donor key cell has a real copy action.
The Received balance wrapped mid-value, so the three browse stat cards rendered 87px high instead of one 60px line and the value baseline no longer matched the other two cards.

The directory search did not recognize a p-prefixed XRP secret or a 32-53 character s-secret, so it hashed the secret text as a brainwallet and opened /key/<sha256(secret)>: a different private key than the one pasted.
The directory search padded any 1-64 hex string to a key (deadbeef became /key/000...deadbeef), while the key page and the donor table treat 1-63 hex characters as brainwallet text.
/keystore-parser matched the old path.indexOf('/key') === 0 test, so its page highlighted the Search nav item instead of Tools.
Every /key chain group except ZEC showed a live balance; the two Zcash rows rendered — because no keyless ZEC provider was wired.
the Solana mnemonic directory rendered — for all 60 rows although a batched getMultipleAccounts provider exists
Chain tabs and cards read colors from separate tables; site.css disagreed with the coordinator on ethereum, tron, litecoin and xrp, and a local symbol table printed ARB/OP/BASE/zkSync instead of ETH.
the BCH mnemonic directory rendered — for all 60 rows although the keyless Haskoin batch endpoint answers 60 addresses per request
the TRON, XRP and SUI mnemonic directories rendered — for every row although the pages already fetched those chains in the private-key directory
XRPScan answered 302 to data.xrpscan.com/tx.json for some accounts; the page followed the redirect into a bulk dataset with no CORS header, so 59 of 60 XRP rows ended in the retry state

Eleven amount formatters and three parsers in ten files reimplemented decimal conversion; five coin() copies converted 18-decimal wei through Number and lost precision above 2^53 (e.g. 2^256-1 wei displayed as a rounded ~1e59).

The seed converter's aggregate line claimed public providers expose no lifetime totals and showed only Active/Sum, although blockchain.info returns total_received in the same balance response it already fetches.

The mnemonic-seeds rows never set data-balance-state/data-balance-at on the row element, so a verifier selecting [data-balance-state] reported 0 rows on a page rendering 60 (a silent-zero measurement).
scripts/density-parity.mjs reported total rows 0 when the row selector matched nothing, indistinguishable from an empty page; the silent zero was read as a measurement.
web/public/site.css, site.js and theme.js drifted from apps/site while web/README.md and projects.json still described byte-identical copies; the committed hashes were stale and nothing failed CI.

Detector ids lived in three diverging markdown tables plus the audit: control-height-scale was {40,44,56} in plan batch 3 and {28,36,44,56} in the gate, table-grammar was absent from plan section 3, field-hero-height was absent from the skill table, and status-pill-geometry allowed 18px while the spec said 20.
A detector registry edit could leave the generated tables in SKILL.md, DESIGN-SYSTEM.md and plan.md stale, so the human docs described rules the gate no longer enforced.
The 60-row /private-keys/bitcoin-cash directory rendered — for every balance although the shared batched Haskoin provider already existed and the mnemonic directory used it.

The /key Litecoin and Dogecoin rows showed no balance whenever BlockCypher answered HTTP 429 {"error":"Limits reached."}; both chains had only that one provider although SoChain v3 serves LTC, DOGE and ZEC keyless with CORS. The row attribute recorded only that some provider existed, so the audit stayed green.

SoChain's keyless allowance is 2500 lookups a day per IP (the provider's 429 body says so), not 2500 an hour as the ledger claimed. With the quota exhausted, one 60-row mnemonic page fired 240 SoChain requests (60 addresses x inner retry x outer retry) although every one answered 429, turning one exhausted quota into a self-inflicted storm; ten page loads would exhaust the daily budget for the whole IP.

SoChain answered 429 for every request (retry-after ~11.6 h), so all 60 LTC rows on /mnemonic-seeds/litecoin and /private-keys/litecoin kept the retry state although data/providers.json already declared the keyless litecoinspace Esplora endpoint under litecoin. The shared sochain fetcher stopped at the first 429 and had no fallback, so both directory entry points inherited the dead end.

The new ERC-20 approvals table was not exercised by any detector: ui-audit ran with the vault locked, so 240/240 PASS said nothing about the shared table shell, 44px row actions, Unlimited/Contract/EOA labels or the archive-truncated warning.

A portfolio total could treat a balance that was still loading, failed or never requested as zero, and price a testnet coin at its mainnet ticker, so $0.00 or an inflated USD value looked like a real total.

The allowance grant form was not exercised by any detector: the approvals scenario stopped at the table, so nothing checked its labelled 44px fields, its own visible Unlimited warning line, the zero-amount error state or the rendered unlimited review.

The public puzzle jobs table rendered only when the job store was non-empty, and that state was never audited, so table.puzzle-table shipped without .data-table and the shared 8/12 cell padding and 12px/600 header style; the empty --serve store hid it (issue #261).

The wallet had no transaction history. An EVM address without an indexer would have shown an empty list pretending there was no history, and a new table could have shipped without a detector for its shared shell, 44px action, truncated counterparty title, status pills, loading/empty/error states or the honest EVM-unavailable message.

Choosing a wallet in the built-in WalletConnect modal did not open the wallet app, and the page never exposed the connection URI, so a mobile visitor had to paste it into the wallet's dapp browser. The panel, its deep links, QR, copy action and expired-URI state had no detector.

The .error component hardcoded #ffb3b3 for its text in both themes; on the light theme that is about 1.7:1, so every field error (now load-bearing for the allowance grant) was unreadable. The same literal was copied into .balance-note.err, .directory-hint.err, .global-search-error and .balance-info.err.

The transaction decoder tables built by buildTable in apps/site/tx-page.js also lacked .data-table inside .table-scroll; the rendered audit never sees them because the tables appear only after a decode input, so a static scan now enforces the class in JS builders, HTML and the Rust-embedded markup.
DOGE had no fallback at all when SoChain 429'd, although the SSOT-declared BlockCypher endpoint can serve a batch when its own small quota has room.
The puzzle detail action row omitted the donor Discussion link; the donor target was never recorded.
